messages.content:
You plan the work for one part of a course assignment or project. A team of AI agents will carry
it out: a coding agent builds, a testing agent tests. Design, documentation and the final review are planned
separately, so do not add those steps.

Return JSON with "steps", "research_questions", "not_plannable" and "open_questions".

Each step:
- key: a short local name ("b1", "b2" for build steps, "t1", "t2" for test steps).
- title: an imperative title of at most 8 words ("Broadcast messages to all clients").
- description: one or two sentences on what to do.
- phase: "implement" (build something) or "test" (check that it works).
- requirement_ids: the ids of the requirements the step delivers or checks. Use only ids from the list.
- acceptance_criteria: 1-4 concrete, checkable statements taken from the requirements, keeping their numbers
  ("at least 10 clients connected at the same time").
- effort_hours: a rough estimate for one student (0.5 to 16).
- depends_on: keys of steps in your answer whose result this step needs (a test needs what it tests; the client
  may need the server's protocol). Never depend on a later step in a circle.
- group: a 1-3 word feature name shared by related steps ("Messaging").

Rules:
- Every requirement id in the list must appear in at least one step, unless it is in not_plannable.
- Use as few steps as the work needs: a build step covers 1-4 closely related requirements that one person would
  build together; a test step checks one feature group (it may check several build steps).
- Quality requirements (speed, robustness, usability) usually belong to test steps.
- Writing tests, scripts or documents that a requirement asks for is a build step.
- Dependencies: a step that uses, extends, tests or describes what another step makes depends on it (the command-line
  interface needs the logic it calls; unit tests need the code they test; code implementing a model needs the model).
- At most 12 steps. Never invent requirements, numbers, tools or extra features.
- research_questions: 2-5 specific questions the team must answer before designing (techniques, libraries the
  constraints allow, known pitfalls).
- not_plannable: requirements an AI agent cannot carry out (a live demo, handing in on a portal), with a reason.
- open_questions: anything unclear or contradictory (an empty list if nothing is).

Project kind: document.
The whole request is one part.

Requirements:
R1 [must, functional] Write a 2000-word report comparing two version control systems.
R2 [must, functional] The report must discuss the branching and merging models of both systems.
R3 [must, functional] Include at least five academic references.
R4 [must, functional] Summarise the findings in a conclusion section.
R5 [could, functional] You may include diagrams of each workflow.

Constraints (respect them, do not make steps for them):
C1 [format] Use APA citation style.
C2 [format] The report may not exceed 2000 words.

This is a writing project: build steps write sections, test steps check them.

response.text:
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "key": "b1",
      "title": "Draft report introduction and overview",
      "description": "Write the opening paragraphs introducing the two version control systems and outline the report structure.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R1"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Report includes a clear introduction of both version control systems",
        "Word count for this section contributes to total ≤ 2000 words"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 2,
      "depends_on": [],
      "group": "Writing"
    },
    {
      "key": "b2",
      "title": "Describe branching and merging models",
      "description": "Compose a detailed comparison of the branching and merging workflows for each system.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R2"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Branching and merging models of both systems are explained",
        "Comparison highlights similarities and differences"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 3,
      "depends_on": ["b1"],
      "group": "Writing"
    },
    {
      "key": "b3",
      "title": "Add academic references in APA style",
      "description": "Insert at least five scholarly citations and format the bibliography according to APA guidelines.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R3"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "At least five academic references are listed",
        "All citations and bibliography follow APA style"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 2,
      "depends_on": ["b1", "b2"],
      "group": "Writing"
    },
    {
      "key": "b4",
      "title": "Write conclusion summarising findings",
      "description": "Summarise the comparative analysis and present final conclusions.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R4"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Conclusion section restates key findings",
        "Conclusion ties back to introduction and analysis"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 1.5,
      "depends_on": ["b2", "b3"],
      "group": "Writing"
    },
    {
      "key": "b5",
      "title": "Create optional workflow diagrams",
      "description": "Design simple diagrams illustrating each system's workflow and embed them in the report.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R5"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Diagrams for both systems are included",
        "Diagrams are clear and labeled"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 1,
      "depends_on": ["b2"],
      "group": "Visuals"
    },
    {
      "key": "t1",
      "title": "Check word count and APA compliance",
      "description": "Verify the full report does not exceed 2000 words and all citations follow APA format.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R3"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Total word count ≤ 2000",
        "APA citation style is correct throughout"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 1,
      "depends_on": ["b1", "b3", "b5"],
      "group": "Quality"
    },
    {
      "key": "t2",
      "title": "Validate branching and merging discussion",
      "description": "Review the section to ensure it fully covers the branching and merging models of both systems.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R2"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Branching and merging models are accurately described",
        "Comparison addresses both systems equally"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 1,
      "depends_on": ["b2"],
      "group": "Quality"
    },
    {
      "key": "t3",
      "title": "Confirm presence of conclusion",
      "description": "Check that a conclusion section exists and reflects the analysis.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R4"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Conclusion section is present",
        "It summarises the main findings"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 0.5,
      "depends_on": ["b4"],
      "group": "Quality"
    },
    {
      "key": "t4",
      "title": "Review optional diagrams",
      "description": "Ensure any included diagrams are correctly labeled and correspond to the described workflows.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R5"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Diagrams are present for both systems",
        "They are correctly referenced in the text"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 0.5,
      "depends_on": ["b5"],
      "group": "Quality"
    }
  ],
  "research_questions": [
    "Which academic databases provide peer‑reviewed articles on version control system comparisons?",
    "What tools (e.g., draw.io, Lucidchart) are allowed for creating workflow diagrams under the project constraints?",
    "Are there any institutional guidelines for APA formatting that differ from the standard manual?"
  ],
  "not_plannable": [],
  "open_questions": []
}
